modeling.status: open - MEASURED 2026-07-30T05:10Z, and the honest headline is that there is NO live breakage today, which the row's framing does not say. FACTS: .env DOES carry a UTF-8 BOM (verified on the raw bytes). 68 Python loaders open it BOM-BLIND against only 2 that use utf-8-sig. The FIRST key in the file is ODDS_API_KEY, so a BOM-blind reader sees '﻿ODDS_API_KEY' and that key is invisible to it. BUT the only two scripts that both load .env AND need ODDS_API_KEY - scripts/odds_snapshot.py and scripts/build_site.py - are BOTH already BOM-safe, so nothing is broken right now. I ALSO RULED OUT THE CONNECTION I WAS TEMPTED TO DRAW: this did NOT cause tonight's odds outage. The poller reads os.environ and never loads .env itself; its PowerShell wrapper does (logging 15 keys loaded) and PowerShell handles a BOM natively. The provider also returned a specific DEACTIVATED_KEY and consumed 42 credits per run, both of which require a key to have been sent. The outage is the payment issue already filed, not this. WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING - THE DEFECT IS POSITIONAL. It silently hides whichever key happens to be FIRST, and which key is first changes any time someone edits .env. So the failure is dormant until an unrelated edit reorders the file, at which point it moves to a new key with no warning. And it presents as 'key absent' - a FATAL 'env var required', or a None flowing into a request - never as a decode error, so it reads as misconfiguration rather than a parsing bug. That is the same absence-reads-as-something-else class as the rest of the 2026-07-30 wake. FIX SHAPE: mechanical - encoding='utf-8-sig' at all 68 sites. Worth doing as ONE sweep in a single lane rather than partially, because the value only arrives when EVERY loader is safe; a partial pass leaves the same latent risk while making the remaining count look smaller than the exposure. I deliberately did not do the free half tonight for that reason. BETTER STILL if it is cheap: give the repo ONE .env loader that every caller imports (the same single-source-of-truth move that fixed the no-prompt env across four git callers tonight), so the encoding is decided once instead of 68 times.

modeling.header: Worktree isolation is largely illusory: 121 modules hardcode the main repo's absolute path
modeling.status: open - MY OWN PREMISE ON THIS ROW WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT ~20 MINUTES AFTER I FILED IT, and the real finding is bigger, so the row is rewritten rather than closed. WRONG: I claimed a worktree lane would lose the gitignored .env and so falsely report the DB unreachable. Refuted three independent ways. (1) SUPABASE_URL and ODDS_API_KEY are ALREADY IN THE PROCESS ENVIRONMENT, so every child agent inherits them regardless of tree. (2) the scripts do not resolve .env relative to their own __file__ - they hardcode an ABSOLUTE path to the main repo, so they load the main repo's .env even from inside a worktree. (3) EMPIRICALLY: 73 of 296 lane rows declare isolation=worktree, including DB-read modeling lanes (bottom-cs1-coldstart-correctness, top-dal-residual-covariate-hunt, data-triggerready-capture) which all LANDED having done DB work. Isolation has been used 73 times and never stranded a credential. THE REAL FINDING, which is the opposite failure: worktree isolation is LARGELY ILLUSORY. 121 .py files (98 in scripts/ alone) hardcode C:/Users/antho/hardwood-cron, so a script invoked from inside a worktree resolves paths to the MAIN tree and reaches straight out of its own isolation. 19 of those 98 also WRITE a file. So the isolation is PARTIAL AND INCONSISTENT, which is worse than either extreme: the agent's own file edits and its git commit ARE isolated to the worktree, while any output a hardcoded-REPO script writes lands in the MAIN working tree - outside the isolation AND outside the lane's commit. Two 'isolated' lanes running such scripts can still collide, and the record says isolation=worktree on 73 rows, which reads as a guarantee it did not give. Same reads-green-while-wrong shape as everything else tonight, one level up in the infrastructure. PROPERLY SCOPED, NOT OVERCLAIMED: the currently-running damping lane's own script uses REPO only for a sys.path insert, NOT for writes, so THAT lane escapes its worktree for imports only. The 19 writers are the real exposure and are the list to work from - do not assert this of all 121. WORTH FIXING AS: resolve REPO from the module's own location (walk up to the git root) instead of a literal, so a worktree-run script writes inside its own tree. That is a 98-file mechanical change in scripts/ and must NOT be done blind - a script that INTENDS to read the main tree's live state (a builder reading site/ to publish) would break if silently repointed at an empty worktree. Classify the 19 writers by intent first. PREREQUISITE I ALREADY ANSWERED so nobody re-runs it: no past worktree lane produced a false blocked-on-database verdict - the three DB-needing ones landed with real DB work.
